skill.name: tdd-vitest-typescript
skill.description: Guides test-driven development for TypeScript projects using Vitest, including setup, test design, mocks, async tests, and refactoring workflows.
skill.summary: Apply Red-Green-Refactor with Vitest and TypeScript for reliable test-first development.
skill.author: Emz1998

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, JavaScript template literals, and sample Vitest assertions. The setup script does have real external command and filesystem side effects, and it accepts an unvalidated target directory before writing generated files.

remediation.suggestion: Normalize projectName, reject absolute paths and parent-directory segments, and keep generated files inside an approved workspace root.
Require explicit user confirmation before running npm commands, and document that npm install can execute dependency lifecycle scripts.
Check whether each target file exists before writing, and prompt before replacing configs, source files, tests, or package.json.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Project Path Can Redirect File Writes
semantic_findings.description: The setup script accepts the target directory from process.argv[2], creates it recursively, changes into it, and writes project files. Absolute paths or parent-directory segments could place generated files outside the intended workspace.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The path comes directly from argv and is passed into existsSync, mkdirSync, and process.chdir before many writes. I found no normalization or rejection of absolute paths or parent traversal.

high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The setup script imports child_process so it can run external commands. The observed commands are setup-related and hardcoded, but this still gives the script package-manager execution capability.

content.value_statement: Teams often add tests late, which makes TypeScript regressions harder to catch. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through test-first Vitest workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains the Red-Green-Refactor cycle for TypeScript features.
Provides Vitest and TypeScript configuration guidance.
Shows examples for unit tests, async tests, mocks, and spies.
Documents reusable patterns for test data, helpers, and parametric tests.
Includes anti-pattern guidance for brittle, flaky, or over-mocked tests.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not full project-specific test architecture by itself.
The setup script can modify files and install npm packages if run.
Examples are illustrative and need adaptation to each codebase.
It does not guarantee complete coverage or defect-free code.

use_cases.title: Start a tested TypeScript feature
use_cases.description: Create the first failing Vitest test, implement the smallest passing code, and refactor with confidence.

use_cases.title: Improve test quality in a code review
use_cases.description: Identify broad assertions, excessive mocks, shared state, and missing edge cases before merging.

use_cases.title: Learn practical TDD patterns
use_cases.description: Practice focused tests, async assertions, fixtures, and coverage habits using TypeScript examples.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Failing Test
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to write the first failing Vitest test for this TypeScript behavior. Then explain the smallest implementation step.

prompt_templates.title: Cover an Existing Function
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for improving current tests.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TypeScript function and propose Vitest tests for normal cases, edge cases, and errors. Follow Red-Green-Refactor.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor with Test Safety
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request before changing production code.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Vitest safety net for this refactor. Prioritize behavior-focused tests and avoid assertions tied to implementation details.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Integration Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an integration testing plan for this TypeScript workflow using Vitest. Separate unit tests, integration tests, mocks, and setup needs.

output_examples.input: I need tests for a calculator divide behavior.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies success and division-by-zero cases, writes the failing test first, then guides the minimal implementation.

output_examples.input: Our async user lookup tests are flaky.
output_examples.output: The skill replaces timing delays with promise-aware assertions, resets mocks between tests, and separates success and failure scenarios.

output_examples.input: Review these Vitest tests before a refactor.
output_examples.output: The skill flags implementation-coupled assertions, suggests behavior-focused coverage, and keeps the refactor protected by meaningful tests.

best_practices: Write the failing test before implementation, then keep each step small.
Test public behavior, edge cases, and error paths instead of private implementation details.
Keep tests isolated by resetting mocks and recreating mutable state per test.
anti_patterns: Do not use broad tests that verify several unrelated behaviors at once.
Do not hide flaky tests with skips or silent error handling.
Do not over-mock internal logic until tests stop proving real behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill install Vitest automatically?
faq.answer: It includes setup guidance and a setup script, but users should review scripts before running them.

faq.question: Can it help with existing code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can add characterization tests, edge-case tests, and refactor safety tests for existing TypeScript code.

faq.question: Does it support async testing?
faq.answer: Yes. The references include promise assertions, rejected promises, retries, and async integration examples.

faq.question: Can it test UI components?
faq.answer: It gives Vitest patterns that can support UI tests, but project-specific rendering tools may still be needed.

faq.question: Is it only for unit tests?
faq.answer: No. It covers unit tests, integration patterns, mocks, fixtures, snapshots, and coverage habits.

faq.question: Will it guarantee complete coverage?
faq.answer: No. It helps design meaningful tests, but teams must choose coverage targets based on product risk.
